title: Latency smoothing phases and guardrail checkpad (Feb 2026 release prep)
content:
Context and intent:
This is a working note for the Feb 2026 micro-release focused on smoothing tail latency after the runtime change (kv-cache rekeying + new kernel selection). The goal is a controlled ramp that preserves p95/p99 SLOs while allowing conservative batching and a small TTL-based cache invalidation. Use this doc as the single-threaded preflight checklist and rollout calendar; escalate unresolved items in #release-ops.

High-level rollout approach (phased ramp):
- Phase 0: Dry-run in staging (2/11–2/12) — smoke, p50/p95 baseline capture, no traffic.
- Phase 1: Internal canary (2/13) — 5% internal traffic, low parallelism, telemetry hook enabled.
- Phase 2: Customer-slice canary (2/14–2/15) — 10% external traffic, split by region (us-east first, eu-west second), throttles at gateway.
- Phase 3: Gradual ramp (2/16–2/18) — 25% -> 50% -> 75% daily step increments depending on signal.
- Phase 4: Full cutover (2/19) — 100% with rollback window and rapid throttles.

Calendared actions (annotated):
- 2/10: Final preflight sync (owner: Caleb) — confirm PR merge readiness, runtime flags, and console feature toggles.
- 2/11: Staging dry-run (owner: SRE lead) — run smoke-sim suite, validate KV rekey paths, export flame graphs.
- 2/12: Telemetry validation (owner: Observability) — ensure new span fields and token-level timing present in traces.
- 2/13: Internal canary (owner: Release steward) — 0900 deploy window, 2h watch, pager rotation.
- 2/14–2/15: Customer-slice canary (owner: Release steward) — US-east 09:00 -> EU-west 13:00, regional fallback tested.
- 2/16–2/18: Ramp cadence daily check-ins 10:00 and 16:00; readiness calls if p99 > threshold.
- 2/19: Full migration final ops checklist and post-mortem kickoff.

Preflight checklist (must be green before Phase 1):
- Code and infra:
  - PRs merged and CI green: REL-4321, infra/kv-cache-rekey.
  - Canary AMIs/images built and verified.
  - Feature flag toggles created (ff/runtime-smoothing-2026-02).
- Observability:
  - p50/p95/p99 dashboards created and pinned (compare baseline from 2/01–2/09).
  - Alert thresholds: auto pause if p99 increases by >20% for two consecutive 5-min windows.
  - Tracing: request path tags include kernel_variant and cache_hit.
- Traffic and capacity:
  - Autoscaler target buffers +20% headroom for 24h after Phase 4.
  - Batching settings conservative default: max_batch_ms=10, max_batch_tokens=1024.
  - Prefix cache TTL set to 30s for initial roll (quick invalidation).
- Safety and fallback:
  - Warm fallback model versions available (model-v1-legacy).
  - Region failover playbook uploaded to confluence.
  - Throttle controller ready with manual overrides.
- Communications:
  - Slack watch channels: #release-ops, #sre-alerts, #product-oncall added.
  - Customer success notified for pilot customers impacted by canary.

Signal matrix (go/no-go heuristics):
- Immediate rollback triggers:
  - p99 request latency > baseline * 1.5 sustained 10m.
  - Error rate (5xx) > 0.5% absolute increase versus baseline over 5m.
  - KV-cache error class observed in > 0.1% of requests.
- Slowdown but keep going signals (investigate, hold):
  - p99 increases 10–50% but rate stable and no 5xx spike.
  - Elevated CPU on a single node type (investigate autoscale).
- Positive progress signals:
  - p95 within ±5% of baseline, p50 improved by >5%.
  - Cache hit ratio above 60% for prefix caching subset.

Runbook snippets (quick ops commands):
- Force fallback to legacy kernel: /ops/release/fallback --to model-v1-legacy --reason "latency spike"
- Reduce batch size globally: /ops/runtime/config --set max_batch_ms=5 --set max_batch_tokens=512
- Temporarily disable prefix caching: /ops/runtime/feature-flag ff/runtime-prefix-cache --off
(ops commands are shorthand for internal runbooks; follow full ACL and audit trail)

Draft release notes (to be refined, customer-facing):
- Summary: Deploy runtime latency-smoothing changes intended to reduce cost variability and improve median throughput. Initial roll includes conservative prefix caching and kernel tuning.
- What changed: The serving runtime will select a new kernel variant for medium-length sequences and enable short TTL prefix caching. This is expected to lower token compute cost for many requests and slightly increase median throughput.
- Impact: During canary we expect no functional changes. Potential transient latency increases may occur during rekeying windows; we will monitor p99 and roll back if necessary.
- Rollout plan: Phased increment from 5% internal to 100% over seven days; customers in the pilot will be contacted directly.
- How to report issues: Open a ticket to REL-4321 or ping #release-ops and include request_id, region, and approximate timestamp.

Open questions / risks to answer before Phase 2:
- Is the new kernel deterministic across GPU types? (owner: infra-kernels)
- Does the cache TTL interact with dedupe/caching in the CDN layer? (owner: platform-network)
- Should we flip the batching config earlier for image-heavy workloads? (owner: applied-ml)

Post-roll tasks (day 0–3 after full cutover):
- Day 0: 2h post-cutover watch, capture heap and kernel counters, save last-known-good config.
- Day 1: Telemetry diff and cost delta report (owner: finance-ops).
- Day 2–3: Sweep customer tickets, prepare retro notes and actionable follow-ups.

Notes to self / quick links:
- Baseline dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/latency-baseline
- Confluence: RELEASE-2026-FEB notes (link in linked_artifacts)
- Slack thread: #release-ops (thread pinned under 2/10 sync)

Bottom line: conservative, observability-first rollout. Keep ramp steps small and use early fallback if p99 shows durable degradation. Use this file as the single source of truth for the watch window; update as signals and decisions occur.
